text:
Predicates:
DeadlyDisease(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is bile duct cancer.
Cholangiocarcinoma(x) ::: x is Cholangiocarcinoma.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is colorectal cancer.
FormOf(x, y) ::: x is a form of y.
WithLowSurvival(x) ::: x has a low survival rate.
IsA(x, y) ::: x is a y.
Premises:
∀x (DeadlyDisease(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: If something is deadly, then it comes with low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) → DeadlyDisease(x) ::: Severe cancers are deadly diseases.
BileDuctCancer(x) → SevereCancer(x) ::: Bile duct cancer is a severe cancer.
∀x (Cholangiocarcinoma(x) → BileDuctCancer(x)) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma is bile duct cancer.
MildFlu(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: Mild flu comes with a low survival rate.
ColorectalCancer(x) → ¬(BileDuctCancer(x) ∧ WithLowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: Colorectal cancer is not both a bile duct cancer and with a low survival rate.
Conclusion:
FormOf(ColorectalCancer, Cholangiocarcinoma) ∧ (IsA(ColorectalCancer, MildFlu) ∨ IsA(ColorectalCancer, BileDuctCancer) ∨ IsA(ColorectalCancer, Cholangiocarcinoma))
